report:
test_total does not fail. It passes. The test that fails is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

I ran the tests (pytest): 2 passed, 1 failed.
- test_plain: pass (399).
- test_total: pass. 399 * 0.9 = 359.1, int() gives 359, the test wants 359.
- test_half_cent_rounds_up: FAIL. assert 959 == 960.

Why it fails:
cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
int() cuts off the fraction. It does not round. 1010 * 0.95 = 959.5, int() gives 959, the test wants 960.
The docstring says "rounded to whole cents", so the code does not do what its docstring says.
This is the same bug as the TODO line: "fix rounding in cart.total (customers see totals one cent short)".

Note for a fix (not done, you asked a question, so I changed nothing):
plain round() would not be enough. Python round() rounds halves to even, so round(959.5) gives 960 but
round(958.5) gives 958. The test wants half up. A half-up rounding on whole cents (for example integer math,
or decimal.Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP) would match the test. Float error is also possible near .5 values,
so integer or Decimal math is the safer choice. Tell me if you want me to fix it.
